title: invariant Examples
concept: Practical invariant examples for common scenarios: range-bound numbers, non-empty collections, valid strings, and cross-field validation.
why: Understanding the common invariant patterns lets you model real-world constraints directly in the type system — making invalid states unrepresentable.
tips: Use invariants to make illegal states unrepresentable — if it compiles, it's valid
Each invariant should check ONE property — compose multiple simple checks
Invariants on type aliases (newtypes) are checked at construction and after every mutation
Cross-field invariants capture business rules that span multiple fields
common_mistakes: Making invariants too complex — they should be quick to check
Forgetting to add invariants to mutable types — mutations can break validity
Assuming others know the invariant — it's enforced, but document WHY it exists
